item.title: Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – No candidate can become Nigeria’s president simply by polling the highest number of votes. The 1999 Constitution also demands that the winner shows support across the federation. Read Also: * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? * 2027: What happens when Nigerian election results are disputed? Also, there is no fixed number of votes that guarantees victory in presidential. Neither 10 million nor 15 million votes means anything on its own. Two conditions are set out in Section 134(2) of the Constitution. A candidate must first have “the highest number of votes cast at the election.” The second condition is the spread. The candidate must have “not less than one-quarter of the votes cast at the election in each of at least two-thirds of all the states in Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.” Nigeria has 36 states, and two-thirds of 36 is 24. The arithmetic is less settled once the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, is counted as a 37th unit, because two-thirds of 37 is about 24.7. Lawyer Femi Falana (SAN) read the provision as meaning “25 states or 24 states plus the FCT”. The Constitution itself says in Section 2(2) that “Nigeria shall be a Federation consisting of States and a Federal Capital Territory.” In 2023 and 1979 The question of whether 25 per cent in Abuja is a separate, compulsory test went to the Supreme Court after the 2023 election. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, argued that Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, had failed it. Tinubu scored about 20 per cent in the FCT, while Obi won the territory. The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, argued that by scoring 25 per cent of the valid votes cast in 29 states, Tinubu had already met the constitutional requirement for presidential election. On Thursday, 26th October 2023, a Supreme Court panel led by Justice Inyang Okoro upheld the lower court’s ruling. The justices held that the FCT has no special status above the states. Under that ruling, 25 per cent in Abuja is not a standalone condition for victory. Section 299 of the Constitution, which treats the FCT as a state, was central to the reasoning. The arithmetic has been fought over before. In 1979, Obafemi Awolowo argued that two-thirds of the then 19 states meant 13 states, and that Shehu Shagari had reached 25 per cent in only 12. The Supreme Court settled that dispute by concluding it would be “12 two-thirds”. That meant 25 per cent in 12 states and 25 per cent of two-thirds of a 13th. When no one meets condition… What happens when nobody meets both conditions is also spelt out in Section 134. INEC must, within seven days of the result, arrange a run-off between two candidates. The first is the presidential candidate with the highest number of votes overall. The second is the candidate with a majority of votes in the highest number of states. item.title: Tinubu’s projects, security efforts boosting South-East economy — Shettima
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said the administration of President Bola Tinubu is driving economic growth and improving security in the South-East through investments in road infrastructure, agriculture, renewable energy, housing and human capital development. Shettima said the Federal Government’s interventions in Ebonyi State and the wider South-East were aimed at improving regional connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and addressing longstanding development challenges. The Vice-President spoke on Monday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, where he urged residents to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the 2027 general elections. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and policies designed to improve citizens’ welfare. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have triumphed over those who mistook the limits of their imagination for the limits of our reach. “We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects and His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. Shettima described public office as a responsibility to deliver measurable improvements in the lives of citizens, adding that the administration was seeking another mandate to consolidate its development programmes. “If any state can speak with confidence about the dividends of democracy, it is Ebonyi. You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. “We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, to defend you, and to stand by you,” he said. Highlighting federal infrastructure investments, the Vice-President listed the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway as one of the major projects expected to strengthen trade and economic integration between the South-East, North-Central and other parts of the country. He also mentioned the Ndibe Bridge, which is designed to connect Ebonyi with Cross River State, as well as ongoing work on the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. According to him, the projects will ease the movement of agricultural produce, manufactured goods and other commodities while reducing transportation challenges for businesses and communities. On agriculture, Shettima described Ebonyi as an important contributor to Nigeria’s food security, particularly in rice and cassava production. He said the Federal Government was supporting farmers through fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and other agricultural development programmes. item.title: PANDEF urges police, DSS to probe political violence in South-South
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA: The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has called on the Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to investigate recent incidents of political violence in Warri and Asaba, Delta State, and Calabar, Cross River State, and prosecute those responsible. The apex socio-political organisation of the South-South region also called for an immediate end to political violence, intimidation and thuggery, warning that such activities were alien to the values and traditions of peaceful coexistence in the region. PANDEF made the call in a statement issued on Monday and signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali. The organisation expressed concern over the incidents, particularly the reported loss of life in Asaba, and described the violence as a threat to peaceful coexistence in the Niger Delta. It specifically cited incidents in the Warri/Effurun axis on September 18, 2026; Calabar on November 4; and Asaba on November 7, 2026. The statement read: “The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) notes with very serious concern and strongly condemns the disturbing incidents of political violence recorded around our region. Most worrisome are the sad events which occurred in the Warri/Effurun axis on Friday, 18th September 2026; in Calabar on Wednesday, 4th November, 2026 and most recently, the incident in Asaba on Saturday, 7th November 2026 in which a life was lost! “Indeed, as the mother body of the peoples of the region, PANDEF views these developments as a sacrilege to our peaceful co-existence in the Niger Delta and strongly condemns them.” Igali said peaceful coexistence, tolerance and political forbearance were values inherited from the region’s founding fathers and must be preserved. He urged political leaders, party supporters and other stakeholders to demonstrate maturity and embrace sportsmanship in resolving political disagreements. The forum also warned political leaders against inflammatory rhetoric, provocation and actions capable of triggering violence, stressing that they had a responsibility to guide their followers. PANDEF particularly appealed to youths in the Niger Delta not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, intimidation or thuggery. It urged young people to channel their energy towards peaceful and constructive political participation rather than serving the interests of selfish political actors. “PANDEF hereby makes a special appeal to the youths of the Niger Delta not to allow themselves to be used as cannon fodders, instruments of political violence, thuggery or intimidation,” the statement added. The organisation further advised political parties to hold rallies and large gatherings in properly secured venues, with adequate security arrangements, particularly during movement to and from event locations. item.title: Fani-Kayode urges South Africa to replace xenophobia with Pan-Africanism
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has called on South Africa to embrace Pan-Africanism and reject xenophobic sentiments that have fuelled attacks on Nigerians and other African nationals in the country. Fani-Kayode made the call on Saturday while speaking at the inaugural Nigerian Fair held at the Nigerian Consulate in Johannesburg. He recalled Nigeria’s contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa, stressing that the liberation movement was a collective African effort. “It wasn’t a black South African struggle. It was a struggle that every nation in Africa led primarily by the frontline states and Nigeria, and every decent civilized nation in the world supported,” he said. The high commissioner urged South Africans not to forget the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. He said Nigeria and the rest of Africa had a stake in South Africa’s development because of their contributions to the country’s liberation. Fani-Kayode described xenophobic attacks as a retrogressive sentiment, urging African countries to strengthen solidarity and cooperation. “We must understand that the world is coming together as one, and we must stand together as one,” he said. He claimed that Nigeria contributed no less than $61 billion to the anti-apartheid struggle between 1960 and 1994, adding that the country also deployed troops to frontline states in support of the campaign against the apartheid regime. He cited the introduction of the “Mandela Tax”, through which Nigerian civil servants contributed financially to the struggle, as one of the country’s solidarity measures. “Nigeria did so much. Mandela tax — we imposed a tax on our own civil servants during the course of the struggle, and that money was channelled to the ANC,” he said. He added that Nigerian schoolchildren also contributed their lunch money to support the struggle, while the country consistently advocated South Africa’s liberation at the United Nations and other international platforms. Fani-Kayode called for stronger ties between Nigeria and South Africa, urging both countries to build bridges of friendship, fraternity and mutual respect. He described perpetrators of xenophobic attacks as a minority driven by what he called Afrophobia and xenophobia. The high commissioner said Nigeria must continue to promote African unity and avoid actions that could further strain relations between the two countries. He also said Nigeria would not sever its economic ties with South Africa despite calls by some Nigerians for such a move, although he acknowledged that patience was wearing thin within the corridors of power. Fani-Kayode assured Nigerians living in South Africa that the Federal Government would continue to take steps to protect their interests and ensure their welfare. item.title: ‎Protect Workers as you grow your businesses, NSITF MD tells entrepreneurs
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — The Managing Director/Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Mr Oluwaseun Faleye, has said that Nigeria cannot develop sustainable, globally competitive enterprises without safeguarding the workers who drive them. ‎ ‎Faleye said this on Monday in his goodwill message at the Grow Nigerian Conference 2026, held at the Ecobank Pan African Centre (EPAC), Victoria Island, Lagos, under the theme “The Next Frontier for Innovation, Policy and Market Access.” ‎ ‎The three-day conference, convened by the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria, SMEDAN under the leadership of Director-General/CEO Mr. Charles Odii, brought representatives of the Federal Government, development partners, business leaders, and entrepreneurs. ‎ ‎While commending SMEDAN for sustaining the platform, Faleye said the theme was timely, as it challenges Nigeria to move beyond business creation to building enterprises that are productive, resilient and capable of generating sustainable employment. ‎ ‎Painting a vivid picture of the Nigerian entrepreneur, Faleye highlighted the manufacturer in Aba struggling to scale, the woman processor in Kano searching for new markets, and the young tech founder in Lagos with global ambitions. He described MSMEs as employers, innovators, and the economic lifeline of families and communities, stressing that they must remain at the heart of Nigeria’s economic transformation agenda. ‎ ‎He, however, acknowledged the harsh operating environment in Nigeria, citing high energy costs, inflation, exchange rate pressures, limited access to affordable financing, inadequate infrastructure and logistics challenges as some of them. ‎According to him: “The challenge is not simply to encourage people to start businesses, but to create an environment in which those businesses can survive, expand, compete and prosper.” ‎ ‎He argued that enterprise development discourse must also answer a critical question: what happens to the people who make those businesses grow? ‎ ‎He said: “Behind every successful enterprise are people whose skills, commitment and labour sustain its operations. A business cannot truly be considered sustainable if its economic success is achieved at the expense of the safety, dignity and wellbeing of its workforce”. ‎ ‎He explained that the NSITF administers the Employees’ Compensation Scheme under the Employees’ Compensation Act, 2010, which provides compensation, medical support, rehabilitation and income replacement to workers who suffer work-related injuries, diseases, disability or death. ‎ ‎Faleye clarified that the scheme is funded by employers’ contribution of one per cent of total monthly payroll, and is not deducted from employees’ salaries. ‎ ‎“Protecting workers is also good for business. item.title: ‘Student is alive’ – Babcock University clarifies viral hall incident
item.description: Babcock University has confirmed that a student involved in an incident at one of its halls of residence is alive and responding to treatment, dismissing reports that he had died. The university, in an official statement signed by Johnson B. Akintayo, AVP, Communication, Media and Branding, said the student was receiving medical attention at the Babcock University Teaching Hospital. Official Statement: Update on the Hall Incident Babcock University confirms that the student involved is alive, responding well to treatment, and receiving the necessary medical care. His parents are on campus with him. Please read the full statement attached. pic.twitter.com/xsMQhWcA2z — Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Nigeria (@Babcock_Univ) November 9, 2026 “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” the statement said. The incident occurred at one of the university’s student residential facilities. According to the institution, the situation was brought under control through the prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose actions prevented a potentially worse outcome. The university also disclosed that one of the students who participated in the rescue sustained injuries and was immediately taken for medical attention. It said the injured student’s parents had been contacted and were on campus to support their son as he received treatment. “The other student who sustained injury while rescuing his roommate, has been treated and discharged,” the statement added. Babcock University said it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. The investigation, it explained, would help determine what happened, identify possible contributing factors and establish measures to prevent a recurrence. The institution also urged members of the public and media organisations to avoid spreading unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations were ongoing. Beyond medical treatment, the university said it was committed to supporting the student’s recovery and well-being. “Babcock University takes the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees seriously,” the statement said. The institution further commended the student’s roommates for their courage and swift intervention, while appealing for sensitivity and restraint in discussions about the incident. It added that it would continue to monitor the student’s recovery and take necessary steps to establish the facts surrounding the incident. item.title: Attempted Suicide: Babcock Student In Viral Video Alive, Receiving Medical Treatment- Management
item.description: The management of Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, has confirmed that a student involved in an incident at one of the institution’s residential facilities is alive and currently receiving medical attention at the university’s teaching hospital. This was communicated in a statement signed by the Associate Vice President, Communication, Media and Branding of the institution, Johnson Akintayo, who dismissed media reports suggesting that the student, whose identity is not disclosed, had died. The university said the student was receiving medical treatment alongside his roommate, who also sustained injuries during the incident. A video that surfaced online on Monday showed a student attempting to jump through the window of one of the university’s hostels as his roommates struggled to prevent him from attempting suicide. Following the incident, some media reports claimed that the student had died. “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” Akintayo said. “The incident was brought under control by the commendable and prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose timely action prevented what could have been a more tragic outcome. “The student with one of his rescuers, however, sustained injuries in the process and were immediately taken for medical attention.” He further stated that the student’s parents had been contacted and were on campus to be with their ward as he receives treatment. Babcock University is a private tertiary institution in South-West Nigeria. (Photo: babcock.edu.ng) According to the statement, the other student who sustained an injury while rescuing his roommate has been “treated and discharged.” The university also disclosed that it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. “This process will help us understand what happened, identify any factors that may have contributed to the situation, and determine appropriate measures to prevent a recurrence.” “The university therefore urges members of the public and media organisations to refrain from circulating unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations are ongoing,” the statement added. “Beyond providing medical attention, the university said it was committed to supporting the student’s full recovery and well-being, adding that it would ensure appropriate support and guidance were made available to facilitate his recovery process ” “Babcock University takes the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees seriously. item.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Rivers and Delta actually show
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Rivers and Delta states, neighbours in the South-South, backed different presidential candidates in the February 25, 2023 election, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Rivers, while Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, won Delta. Rivers: Tinubu ahead by 56,520 votes Tinubu polled 231,591 votes in Rivers, ahead of Obi’s 175,071. That put the APC candidate 56,520 votes clear of the runner-up. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, came third with 88,468 votes. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, trailed with 1,322. Delta: Obi’s commanding lead Delta produced the wider margin. Obi scored 341,866 votes, against 161,600 for Atiku, a lead of 180,266 votes. Tinubu managed 90,183 votes in Delta and finished third. Kwankwaso had 3,122. What the two results show together Taken together, the states reverse each other’s order. Tinubu won Rivers but placed third in Delta, while Obi won Delta and was runner-up in Rivers. Obi was the only candidate to finish in the top two in both states. The combined figures tell a different story from the two state winners alone. Obi polled 516,937 votes across Rivers and Delta, compared with Tinubu’s 321,774. This is a difference of 195,163 votes in Obi’s favour, even though Tinubu took the state with the higher turnout of the two. Obi’s vote in Delta alone, at 341,866, exceeded Tinubu’s combined total for both states by 20,092 votes. Atiku polled 250,068 votes across the two states, finishing third in Rivers and second in Delta. Kwankwaso placed fourth in both, with 4,444 votes combined. Tinubu’s support was uneven. He polled 231,591 votes in Rivers but only 90,183 in Delta, a drop of 141,408 votes between the two neighbouring states. item.title: COP31: WMO warns El Niño could push 2027 temperatures higher
item.description: The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned that 2027 could become the hottest year on record as an unusually strong El Niño combines with the effects of climate change to push global temperatures higher. WMO Secretary-General, Celeste Saulo, gave the warning on Monday while presenting the organisation’s State of the Climate Update 2026 at a news conference during the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye. Saulo said the past 12 years had been the warmest on record, with the last four years, including 2026, ranking as the hottest. She disclosed that global average temperatures between January and September 2026 were approximately 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. According to her, the developing 2026/2027 El Niño is unusually strong, with sea-surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific expected to approach four times the 0.5-degree threshold used to declare the climate phenomenon. “Indeed, this 2026/2027 El Niño is off the charts. It is different from any El Niño that we have monitored,” she said. The WMO chief explained that El Niño typically has its greatest impact on global temperatures in the following year, raising concerns that 2027 could surpass previous temperature records. She also revealed that ocean heat content had reached a record high for the 10th consecutive year, while global sea levels had risen to unprecedented levels, exposing about 900 million people living in low-lying coastal areas to increasing risks. Saulo warned that extreme heat, tropical cyclones and intense rainstorms were becoming more severe, exposing millions of people to dangerous weather conditions in 2026. She cited heatwaves across India, Pakistan, other parts of Asia and North America, as well as tens of thousands of excess deaths recorded in Europe. “The human and economic cost is unacceptably high,” she said. Saulo called on governments participating in COP31 to strengthen global climate observation systems and increase funding for early-warning mechanisms. She noted that the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early-warning systems had increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. “We cannot afford to fly blind,” she said, emphasising the need for sustained climate monitoring to anticipate extreme weather events and protect vulnerable populations. Also speaking, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary, Simon Stiell, described the climate crisis as a global health emergency, warning that extreme heat, pollution and climate-related disasters were placing increasing pressure on healthcare systems. Stiell said heatwaves during the northern hemisphere’s summer had killed an estimated 50,000 people across Europe, while hundreds of millions of people in southern Asia were exposed to extreme heat. “The climate crisis is now a global health crisis of pandemic proportions,” he said. item.title: Full list: Messi makes FIFPRO World 11 as Ronaldo misses out
item.description: Lionel Messi has been named in the 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11, extending his record as the most-selected player in the award’s history, while Cristiano Ronaldo failed to make the final team. Messi returns to the prestigious team for the first time since 2023, taking his record number of appearances to 18. The Argentine first made the selection in 2007 and has continued to earn recognition from fellow professional footballers across successive generations. Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal also made history after becoming the first player to earn two FIFPRO World 11 selections before turning 20. The Spain international was also included in last year’s team. Yamal joins fellow Spanish players David Raya, Pau Cubarsi and Rodri in the 2026 selection, taking Spain’s record tally of Men’s World 11 appearances to 53. The team was unveiled following votes from 19,806 professional male footballers across 73 countries, making it one of the few major football awards decided exclusively by players. Since 2005, FIFPRO has invited professional footballers worldwide to vote for the players they believe have delivered the most impressive performances during the assessment period. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain) Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco) Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England) Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain) Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway) Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France) Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina) Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) How the voting worked Professional footballers cast their votes through a secure digital platform provided by FIFPRO and its affiliated player unions. For the 2026 edition, players were assessed based on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026. To qualify, footballers must have featured in at least 30 official matches during the period. Each voter selected their three best performers in four categories: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward. The goalkeeper and the three players with the most votes in each of the defensive, midfield and attacking categories secured their places in the team. The final position was awarded to the remaining outfield player with the highest number of votes. item.title: Ethiopian Airlines, Air Peace sign interline agreement to boost connectivity
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Africa’s leading aviation group, Ethiopian Airlines, and Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, have signed a bilateral interline agreement, strengthening air transport connectivity across Africa and expanding travel opportunities for passengers. The partnership enables each airline to issue tickets for eligible itineraries that include flights operated by both carriers, providing customers with a more convenient and integrated travel experience. Through this collaboration, passengers will be able to book qualifying journeys on a single ticket and enjoy through-checked baggage to their destination, where applicable. Commenting on the partnership, Ethiopian Airlines Group Mr Mesfin Tasew, said “We are delighted to partner with Air Peace, a leading carrier in Nigeria, through this strategic interline agreement. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to enhancing connectivity, improving customer convenience, and supporting the growth of air travel across the African continent. By combining our strengths, we are creating more travel opportunities and bringing Africa closer to the world.” For his part, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace, Allen Onyema, said: “This partnership with Ethiopian Airlines represents another significant milestone in our commitment to strengthening Africa’s aviation connectivity and bringing the continent closer together. By combining Air Peace’s extensive domestic, regional network, and our growing international network with Ethiopian Airlines’ global reach, we are creating greater opportunities for seamless travel in and out of the African continent. Beyond expanding travel options, this collaboration reflects our shared vision of fostering stronger economic, commercial and cultural ties across Africa and beyond. At Air Peace, we remain committed to building strategic partnerships that enhance passenger convenience, broaden connectivity and position African aviation as a formidable force in global air transport.” Meanwhile, the streamlined process eliminates the need for separate bookings and baggage re-checks, creating a smoother and more efficient travel experience. The agreement links Air Peace’s domestic and regional network with Ethiopian Airlines’ vast international network spanning Africa, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas. As a result, travellers departing from major Nigerian and west African cities will gain seamless access to Ethiopian Airlines’ global destinations through Addis Ababa, while international passengers arriving on Ethiopian Airlines flights will benefit from expanded onward travel options across Nigeria and west africa through Air Peace’s domestic network. item.title: Wike criticises ADC over reaction to court judgment
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, on Monday criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) over its comments on the court judgment that removed the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the party. Wike spoke at a town hall interactive meeting with political stakeholders, traditional rulers and residents of Kwali Area Council of the FCT. He said political parties should serve as vehicles for development and good governance rather than platforms for persistent internal conflicts. The minister also accused opposition politicians of placing personal ambitions above the welfare and development of the people. “Isn’t it that a party is a vehicle that you enter intentionally to go where you are going? When you get there, you talk about development, you talk about good governance, and how you can bring welfare to your people,” he said. Wike commended area council chairmen and political leaders across party lines who had agreed to work together in the interest of the FCT. He urged residents to reject politicians who only appear during election periods with promises, calling on them to support leaders whose performance could be assessed through infrastructure delivery and empowerment initiatives. The minister said the administration of President Bola Tinubu had taken steps to address the country’s economic challenges and grant the FCT greater administrative autonomy. He cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, appointment of an indigene of the territory as Head of Service and removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account (TSA) as examples of the administration’s achievements. Wike assured residents that the administration would take difficult decisions where necessary to deliver critical infrastructure, complete abandoned road projects and expand political representation for the people of the FCT. The meeting was attended by the Executive Chairman of Kwali Area Council, Nuhu Daniel Kwali; traditional rulers led by the Etsu of Kwali, Luka Ayedoo Nizassan III; councillors and representatives of the six area councils of the FCT. item.title: 2027: APC govt has built Nigeria for the benefit of few – Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of building a country that works only for those in power, challenging the ruling government to explain what it has achieved for Nigerians in three years. Makinde said the administration had failed to deliver a country that worked for ordinary Nigerians, alleging that its newly promoted reform agenda merely repackaged ideas already advanced by the APM. He urged voters to reject what he described as a government serving the interests of a privileged few. Speaking on Monday at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Jos, Plateau State, the former Oyo State governor accused the ruling government of appropriating his party’s ideas. “When we unveiled our RESET Agenda, I said in Abuja that they would soon start stealing our ideas. Now they have started. They say theirs is ‘Reform to Prosperity’. They now say they want a Nigeria that will work for everybody. What have they been doing over the past three years? “They have built a Nigeria that works only for them. Send the oppressors packing. Send them back to Lagos, and let us bring in the team that will reset Nigeria,” he said. Makinde identified insecurity as a major obstacle to Plateau’s economic potential, promising that an APM government would prioritise security, tourism and job creation. Reflecting on his experience of Jos’s pleasant evening weather, he said the state could become a major tourism destination if its security challenges were addressed. “Security is a major pillar of the RESET Agenda. Once we start attracting tourists, our economy on the Plateau will expand, and we will create jobs for our teeming youths,” he said. Urging supporters to take the party’s message to the grassroots, Makinde stressed that electoral victories were determined at polling-unit level. “Go back to your various units and spread the RESET message. Elections are won at the unit level. Go back to your units with the RESET message. If Nigeria is not working for you, then let us reset it. When we reset Nigeria, we will have a country that works for everybody,” he said. Earlier, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, appealed to Plateau residents to support the APM, lamenting that insecurity had eroded the state’s reputation as a peaceful tourism destination. Recalling his frequent visits to the state in the past, Daura said the party was determined to restore its lost appeal. “Plateau has been a state of peace and tranquillity, a home of tourism where anything good used to be found. Personally, years back, I used to visit the Plateau at least three times a year. Unfortunately, some people have tried to spoil the Plateau. But we are here with our resolute agenda to set things right for the Plateau and for Nigeria,” he said. item.title: Toluwanisings laid to rest in Ibadan
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of his family over his final resting place. The gospel artiste was buried on Monday, November 9, 2026, in a private ceremony attended by family members following a funeral service at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, Alakia, Ibadan. His burial came after a disagreement between his widow, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his paternal relatives over where his remains should be interred. While his paternal family had expressed concerns about the circumstances surrounding his death and initially pushed for his burial in Ikirun, Osun State, his widow and associates were involved in discussions over the final arrangements. The disagreement attracted public attention and eventually prompted the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command. On November 3, the parties involved signed a peace undertaking at the police command headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, agreeing to avoid further public exchanges and actions capable of escalating tensions. Speaking on the agreement, the police command stated that, “All parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace.” The intervention paved the way for the family to settle on burying the singer at his Ibadan residence, where his wife and children live. Toluwanisings, who was widely recognised for his energetic worship ministrations and gospel songs, including A Very Big God, died on October 14, 2026. His death generated reactions across the gospel music community, while the disagreement surrounding his burial further drew public attention to the family’s situation. item.title: 2027 will test clarity of Nigeria’s legal framework on electoral justice – INEC
item.description: …warns AI, digital threats may spill into courtrooms … as 375 tribunal judges take oath By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Monday said the 2027 general elections would test not only its operational preparedness but also the effectiveness and clarity of the nation’s legal framework for electoral justice. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. The Chairman of the electoral body, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening ceremony of a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the 2027 election petition tribunals held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. The workshop was preceded by the inauguration of 375 judges who will serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. It depends equally on public confidence that electoral disputes will be determined independently, fairly and in accordance with the law. “Citizens must be assured not only that their votes count, but also that the legal system is capable of protecting their democratic choices. “The consequences of electoral judgments frequently extend beyond candidates and political parties. They affect public confidence, the legitimacy of elected institutions and democratic stability. “Judicial scrutiny also provides an important mechanism of accountability for election administration. item.title: Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Political economist Pat Utomi has accused the APC-led government of abandoning its responsibilities while Nigerians pay out of pocket for basic services, from electricity and water to roads, healthcare and education. In a post on his X handle on Monday, Utomi questioned what citizens receive in return for paying taxes when households and communities must fund services that government is expected to provide. “The only thing this APC-led government is good at doing is making your life worse,” he wrote. Utomi said Nigerians buy generators to cope with unreliable electricity, sink boreholes for water and contribute money to repair roads. He also cited private security, healthcare and schools as costs families increasingly bear because public institutions have been neglected. He added that waste disposal, drainage, streetlights and transformers had also become private financial responsibilities. “Then what exactly are we paying this APC-led government to do?” he asked, arguing that governments elsewhere invest public resources in education, healthcare, infrastructure and social welfare. Utomi also criticised the government’s appeals for patience and sacrifice amid economic hardship. He cited the removal of petrol subsidies and increases in electricity tariffs and university fees, alongside rising healthcare costs. “But how much more must the people sacrifice while those in power continue to enjoy the privileges of office?” he asked. Utomi argued that taxation obliges government to provide public services, describing it as more than a contribution from citizens to politicians. “The government cannot collect from the people, abandon its responsibilities and then demand applause from the people they’re making their lives difficult,” he wrote. He concluded with a challenge to the government: “If Nigerians must finance their own survival, what exactly is the purpose of government?” In a separate post on Sunday, Utomi said the APC government had made the daily struggle to earn a living an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. He described the hardship as a tragedy for a richly endowed nation that he believes is poorly governed. He said: “The incompetence of the APC government has turned the daily struggle for survival into an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. Those who labour honestly to earn a living are being punished by a system that should be making their lives easier. What a tragedy for a nation so richly endowed yet so poorly governed!” The post Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: British Comedian Russell Brand Jailed 10 Years For Rape, Assault
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences, including rape as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as Judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims who had suffered significant and lasting harm. Paying tribute to the “bravery” of the women who came forward, the judge told Brand he had acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. His wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK” as he was led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Laura Gallacher (C), the wife of British comedian and actor Russell Brand is helped into a car after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) The sentence marks the final fall in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. The woman said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years, as his star was rising, it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. Brand listened impassively, looking straight ahead. ‘Celebrated’ Russell Brand’s father ”Ron” Brand (L) leaves the court building after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand takes place at Southwark Crown Court in south London on November 9, 2026.(Photo by JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP) A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said, adding the consequences of the rape had “affected almost every aspect of my life”. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the victims’ bravery would bring about wider changes to the legal system. Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims, including setting up teams in every police force for handling rapes and serious sexual offences. item.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
item.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. China’s Hangyu Zhang (L), silver medalist; Nigeria’s Gift Bright (C), gold medalist; and Poland’s Szymon Dolega (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the men’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. item.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded,” he said. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation, or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect, and our shared humanity take,” he said. item.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
item.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. The commission also recommended disciplinary action against some public officials suspected of assisting the alleged scheme. In October 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja struck out the initial eight-count charge after jurisdictional concerns prompted the Attorney-General of the Federation to withdraw the case.
